A drawback of the NFFRCISTG model described in @sec-network-causal-inference is that it assumes patterns of causal interference are known. As a consequence, it is not possible to acknowledge the inherent uncertainty in our understanding of the network and, moreso, our measurement of it. 

In this section of the appendix, we extend the NFFRCISTG model by allowing for the inclusion of two classes of observational unit — people and places — and by allowing the relationships between people and places to be randomly generated by the [causal model](#def-causal-model). We name this the [Bipartite Random Network FFRCISTG model (BRNFFRCISTG)](#def-brnffrcistg).  It is a [causal model](#def-causal-model) that includes one or more [*graph generators*](#def-npsem-ne) — matrices of relational variables that model the network edges as random variables, one for each ordered pair of observational units, since influence need not run both ways. We also give two restrictions on how people's ties to places form, which make the network's law estimable from one realization: local row formation and, for ties formed dyad by dyad, the [DBRNFFRCISTG](#def-dbrnffrcistg). [Nonparametric identification and estimation](#sec-identification-estimation) uses them.  

Before outlining the [BRNFFRCISTG](#def-brnffrcistg), we introduce new tools -- the causal directed acyclic network graph (DANG), the single world intervention network graph (SWING), and the random network NPSEM.
